subject: Urgent: p95/p99 latency spikes on 16k+ requests — immediate mitigation requested
messages:
From: Carlos Ortega <c.ortega@nimbushealth.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: eng+prod@nimbushealth.com
Date: Sun, 7 Mar 2026 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Severe latency regressions - affecting production

Laura —

We started seeing a severe tail-latency regression on our Redwood-hosted integration starting ~03:00 UTC today. Key observations: p95 latency is ~2.2x baseline and p99 is ~4x baseline, requests are timing out (504) and some retries are compounding the queue. This began right after the model variant update you rolled out at ~02:45 UTC.

It looks correlated with long-context requests (we're sending a lot of 16k and some 32k documents for medical-note summarization). Attached is a short excerpt of request traces (nimbus_latency_excerpt_20260307.log) showing request timestamps, model variant id, and error codes.

This is impacting production processing for our nightly ingestion pipelines and causing SLA violations. We need immediate mitigation: either rollback the model variant, throttle long-context requests, or route them to a different pool. Our engineering team is available to run tests with you.

We also need executive visibility — this is causing customer impact. Please advise next steps and an emergency action plan.

Thanks,
Carlos Ortega

On Sun, Mar 7, 2026 at 2:12 PM Carlos Ortega <c.ortega@nimbushealth.com> wrote:
> Laura —
> 
> We started seeing a severe tail-latency regression on our Redwood-hosted integration starting ~03:00 UTC today...

Quick triage notes (initial):
- Reproduced a p99 tail using a replay of Nimbus's 16k/32k requests in staging.
- Root cause appears to be load-wave interactions with the serving scheduler + increased KV cache misses for long prefixes. When sequence lengths spike, some workers are thrashing memory (GPU memory fragmentation) which spikes serialization and queue latency.
- The new model variant uses a different attention kernel that amplifies per-token exec time at very long contexts in our current kernel selection path.

Immediate mitigations I can push right now (need approval from Marcus/Evelyn to touch traffic routing):
1) Enable prefix/KV cache bypass fallback and tune cache retention for large contexts (low risk).
2) Temporarily cap hosted tier maximum context to 8k for best-effort routing and route >8k to a specialized variant with long-context optimizations in a separate pool (requires routing rule change).
3) Add a circuit-breaker: reject (429) requests >24k with clear retry-after header to prevent queue clogging.
4) If we need capacity fast, enable emergency burst on Dedicated pool (higher cost) and route the 16k/32k workload there for 6–12 hours.

I’ll prepare the config diff and the canary plan. Marcus/Evelyn — if you OK the routing rules, I’ll apply the prefix-cache change immediately and monitor p95/p99.

—Jonas
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Ortega <c.ortega@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Severe latency regressions - affecting production

Carlos —

Very sorry for the impact. We recommend the following customer-facing short-term plan (if you approve):
- Immediate: we will throttle incoming 32k requests and route 16k requests to a specialized long-context pool (expect 15–30 min implementation).
- Mitigation verify: we will run a post-change replay and share a p95/p99 snapshot within 60 minutes of the change.
- Compensation: offer a one-time credit for the impacted windows and an operational review once things are stable.

Can you confirm you’re OK with temporary throttling of 32k and routing 16k to the long-context pool? We’ll hold the rollback option as a fallback if the routing doesn't fully mitigate.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Markus / Evelyn —

Summary: Nimbus Health (DEAL-7890) reported p95/p99 regressions on long-context (16k/32k) requests starting 03/07 UTC after our model variant rollout. Engineering (Jonas) recommends: enable prefix-caching tweaks immediately, cap hosted context to 8k, route 16k->dedicated long-context pool, and add a circuit-breaker for >24k. Customer-facing mitigation (Vanessa) is ready to throttle 32k and run verification.

Ask:
- Approve emergency routing change + prefix-cache tweak (low risk) — immediate.
- Approve enabling Dedicated burst capacity for 12 hours to offload 16k/32k traffic if routing alone is insufficient. Estimated incremental cost: ~$1,800/hr while active.

If we do not make changes now, Nimbus will continue to see SLA violations. They have asked for executive visibility and a remediation ETA. Please reply with OK / NO-OK / QUESTIONS so we can proceed.

—
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales

From: Carlos Ortega <c.ortega@nimbushealth.com>

Date: Mon, 9 Mar 2026 09:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Severe latency regressions - affecting production

Laura / Vanessa —

Thanks for the quick response. We approved the temporary throttling and the routing change. After your team applied the prefix caching tweak and routed 16k traffic to the long-context pool, our p95/p99 numbers returned to baseline within ~45 minutes. Attached is the post-mitigation report (nimbus_post_mitigation_p95_report_20260309.pdf).

We still want a follow-up:
- A durable fix for long-context workloads (kernel/quantization path work).
- A documented traffic policy for context length (recommended thresholds and retry semantics).
- A post-mortem and timeline for the root cause fix.

We appreciate the rapid help — please confirm a follow-up meeting by EOD.

Regards,
Carlos Ortega
Head of Platform, Nimbus Health
